### Step 1: Source-Reference Alignment & Semantic Analysis
Perform a word-by-word alignment between the Source Text and the Reference Translation.
Goal: Identify the specific English meaning and precise semantic definition for each Source token in this context.
Instructions: 1. Use Reference for Context: Use the Reference Translation to disambiguate polysemous words. 2. Define Semantics: For the [Contextual Definition] column, write the specific dictionary definition that applies to this context. - Example: For "trattar", do not just write "treat". Write "to discuss; to deal with a subject". - Example: For "ben", write "the good; virtue". 3. Analyze Grammar: Identify the grammatical role (Subject, Direct Object, etc.).
Table Columns: - [Source Word] - [Morphology] (Lemma, POS) - [English Equivalent] (Literal word aligned with Source) - [Contextual Definition] (Specific dictionary sense used here) - [Grammatical Role] (Syntactic function)
Source Text: 1 Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita 2 mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, 3 ché la diritta via era smarrita.
Reference Translation (English): Midway upon the road of our life I found myself within a dark wood, for the right way had been missed.

*Notes*
* The Italian poem is Dante’s **Divine Comedy** (Inferno, Canto I, line 1‑3). * The English reference (“Midway upon the road of our life …”) is a 19th‑century translation; the literal equivalents above stay as close as possible to the original Italian wording while providing the precise sense required by the context.
